zh: 大家好，我是余秋雨，我们继续讲课。
en: Hello everyone, I am Yu Qiuyu. Let us continue with our lectures.

zhSentences.text: 大家好，我是余秋雨，
我们继续讲课。

enSentences.text: Hello everyone, I am Yu Qiuyu.
Let us continue with our lectures.

zh: 上次我把老子的行于大道，相反相成，无为而治，和光同尘，直到最后的韬光养晦，这整整的思维，最后概括成一个非常具有高度的思想，叫做上善若水，他不是计谋，他是一个至善，和阴谋正好相反的。这个正是我们对老子有一种重新认识了，我上次结束的时候讲，我这一生有好多世界上著名的思想曾经帮助过我，但是对我帮助最大的是老子的上善若水，滋润万物而不争，一向处于低位，很安静地对着万物微笑的这种思维是最好的思维，这对我帮助很大。
en: Last time, I summarized Laozi's entire philosophical continuum—walking the Great Dao, opposites complementing each other, governing through non-action, softening glare to merge with dust, and concealing brilliance—into a sublime overarching principle known as "Supreme Good Is Like Water"; it is not a calculated maneuver, but supreme virtue, the exact opposite of conspiracy. This gives us a renewed understanding of Laozi; as I mentioned at the close of last lecture, many world-renowned philosophies have aided me throughout my life, yet none has helped me more profoundly than Laozi's insight of being like water—nourishing all things without contending, willingly resting in lowly places, and smiling quietly upon all creation—which has been of tremendous help to me.

zh: 恢复老子哲学的真面目
en: Restoring the True Face of Laozi's Philosophy

zh: 在我的一生当中，很多很多困惑，因为这个哲学就可以迎刃而解。经常有学生问我，老师你为什么无视高位的诱惑，无视外来的各种挑衅，还能够坚持天天写作，写作几十年，书一本本地出，完全不理会外面的喧闹，你怎么能够做到这样？而且不理会外面的诱惑，什么协会也不参加，什么会也不参与，怎么会是这样？
en: Throughout my life, myriad perplexities have been effortlessly resolved because of this philosophy. Students often ask me: "Teacher, why do you ignore the temptations of high office and external provocations, yet persist in writing day after day for decades, publishing book after book while completely ignoring outside tumult—how do you manage that?" "And you ignore worldly allurements, joining no associations and attending no conferences—how can you be like this?"

"And you ignore worldly allurements, joining no associations and attending no conferences—how can you be like this?"

zh: 我对学生总是淡淡的一笑，然后就讲水，讲老子的水。学生们就会问，他说老师你既然讲到水，我们就想起了一个比喻，中国的一个成语，叫水滴石穿，你是不是用水的方式，把石头滴穿它，你就胜利了。我说不对，这里边没有胜利这一说。因为水滴石穿这个思维，水并没有把石头当作敌人、当作对手，甚至于根本没有把石头当作对象；穿石，或者说石穿，并不是预计的设计，而是自然的安排。这个自然的安排，就是天体自然的安排，这就是道了。
en: I always give my students a gentle smile, and then I speak of water—Laozi's water. The students would then ask: "Teacher, since you speak of water, we are reminded of a Chinese idiom—'water drops pierce stone'; do you use the way of water to penetrate the rock and achieve victory?" I reply: no, there is no such concept as 'victory' here. In the true philosophy of water dripping through stone, water never treats the rock as an enemy, a rival, or even an object of confrontation; piercing the stone is not a premeditated calculation, but a natural unfoldment. This natural unfoldment is the cosmic order of nature itself—this is the Dao.

zh: 我们慢慢地写，慢慢地讲，几十年的时间把什么东西弄穿了，这不是我们的目标，因为我们并不觉得眼前有块石头是我们的斗争对象，我一定要慢慢地动用水滴把它滴穿，如果是这样的话，我那个水滴也太慢了，我为什么不做水，我们做个大力士把石头搬走，这不就干脆一点吗？这里边不存在我们想象的一个长时间躲起来的谋略，和一个对手周旋，最后安静的我方却反而胜利了。因为按照老子的哲学，没有胜败，我们只是滋润万物而已。
en: Writing slowly and lecturing steadily across decades until something is penetrated has never been our objective, because we never view an obstacle before us as an adversary to be conquered by dripping water; if that were our intent, dripping water would be far too slow—why not simply become a strongman and haul the rock away? Wouldn't that be far more direct? There is no calculated scheme of lying low for years to outmaneuver an opponent so that our quiet side ultimately claims victory. Because in Laozi's philosophy, there is neither victory nor defeat; we simply nourish all living things.

zh: 我这么讲讲以后，大家就明白了，我们不能把老子的大善变成大伪，虚伪的伪，也不能把老子的大道变成邪道。我看到很多很多的有学问的学者，他们在写老子的时候，都笑眯眯的说，老子是个老滑头，老子是个阴谋家等等，这都搞错了，这是很对不起老子。
en: Once I explain it this way, everyone understands: we must never degrade Laozi's supreme benevolence into hypocrisy, nor twist Laozi's Great Dao into devious craftiness. I have seen many erudite scholars write about Laozi and remark with a smirk that he was a "crafty old fox" or a "master conspirator"; this is completely mistaken and does a profound disservice to Laozi.

zh: 老子是利万物而不争的思维的提出者，是上善若水的提出者，所以，我作为一个学者，作为一个文化人，恢复老子的本意，是一种学术责任，更是一种道义责任。尤其我自己受到老子那么好的影响，这就成了一种生命的责任了。我想我的学员也应该如此，我们正面地来理解老子的了不起的上善思维。
en: Laozi is the visionary who propounded that the supreme good benefits all things without contention and is like water; thus, as a scholar and a cultural practitioner, restoring Laozi's authentic intent is both an academic duty and a moral obligation. Having personally received such profound guidance from Laozi, this has become a life's solemn duty. I believe my students should do the same: we should understand Laozi's marvelous philosophy of the Supreme Good with positive clarity.

zh: 我们中国文化当中，阴谋论的东西很多，其实从中国历史上阴谋没那么多，至少没有我们现在电视剧里所写的那么多，没那么多，所以我经常给纽约的朋友讲，到纽约讲课，我有几个纽约的朋友说，我也想了解中国文化，我们终于看了已经翻译成英文的中国的有几个电视剧，一看以后吓坏了，中国怎么有那么多那么多的阴谋，这宫廷上下，每一个台阶，每一张笑脸，每一个美丽的宫女都是阴谋家。
en: Conspiracy theories abound in Chinese cultural folklore, yet historically speaking, conspiracies were never that rampant—certainly nowhere near as ubiquitous as modern television dramas portray. I often mention this when lecturing to friends in New York; several New York friends told me: "We wanted to learn about Chinese culture, so we watched a few Chinese TV series translated into English, and we were utterly terrified." "Why are there so many endless conspiracies in China? In those royal courts, every step, every smile, and every beautiful palace maid turns out to be a scheming conspirator!"

zhSentences.text: 我们中国文化当中，阴谋论的东西很多，其实从中国历史上阴谋没那么多，至少没有我们现在电视剧里所写的那么多，没那么多。
所以我经常给纽约的朋友讲，到纽约讲课，我有几个纽约的朋友说，我也想了解中国文化，我们终于看了已经翻译成英文的中国的有几个电视剧，一看以后吓坏了。
中国怎么有那么多那么多的阴谋，这宫廷上下，每一个台阶，每一张笑脸，每一个美丽的宫女都是阴谋家。

enSentences.text: Conspiracy theories abound in Chinese cultural folklore, yet historically speaking, conspiracies were never that rampant—certainly nowhere near as ubiquitous as modern television dramas portray.

I often mention this when lecturing to friends in New York; several New York friends told me: "We wanted to learn about Chinese culture, so we watched a few Chinese TV series translated into English, and we were utterly terrified."
"Why are there so many endless conspiracies in China? In those royal courts, every step, every smile, and every beautiful palace maid turns out to be a scheming conspirator!"

zh: 我说，不是，中国阴谋没那么多，这是过去官方的史学家，后来我们可爱的当代的编剧想象出来的。我说，你看中国的历史书上确实写了很多阴谋，但是几百年就那么几个阴谋，这个阴谋中国老百姓不知道，因为在很长的时间，中国老百姓还是文盲更多一点，他们完全读不懂，看不清楚。我说我小的时候在农村，后来长时间在农村劳动，在文革当中也在农场劳动，我非常了解中国农民，我告诉纽约的朋友，中国的农民真的阴谋不多。他们的缺点呢，是比较吝啬，比较小气，不讲卫生，就这么几个缺点，很少有阴谋，如果说有阴谋的话，可能是有一点攀比，有一点保守，如此而已。
en: I answered: no, China did not have that many conspiracies; those were exaggerated by imperial historians of the past and later magnified by our imaginative contemporary screenwriters. I said: while Chinese history books indeed record conspiracies, there were only a handful across several centuries, and common folk were oblivious to them because for centuries widespread illiteracy kept people completely detached from court intrigues. I shared that I grew up in the countryside, labored in rural villages for years, and worked on agricultural farms during the Cultural Revolution; I know Chinese peasants intimately, and I assured my New York friends that ordinary Chinese farmers harbor virtually no conspiracies. Their shortcomings might be petty frugality, stinginess, or neglect of hygiene—just those few human foibles—with hardly any deceit; at most, they might indulge in a little neighborhood rivalry or conservative caution, and that is all.

zh: 在这个问题上，我们在学习中国哲学的时候，一定要明白，我们的首席哲学家老子，把他歪曲成阴谋家是错的。他是一个传播最高道德的人，水利万物而不争，是这样的一个思维，中国应该普及这样的思维到我们的生活当中去。我们的无为而治不是阴谋，我们的相反相成不是阴谋，我们韬光养晦也不是阴谋，理由是，老子不是阴谋家。这样我就把老子已经讲得比较完整了。
en: On this point, as we study Chinese philosophy, we must realize that distorting our premier philosopher Laozi into a conspirator is completely wrong. He was an apostle of supreme morality whose core insight—that water benefits all things without contending—ought to be embraced and popularized in our everyday lives. Governing through non-action is not a conspiracy, opposites complementing each other is not a conspiracy, and cultivating strength quietly is not a conspiracy—for the simple reason that Laozi was never a schemer. With this, I have presented Laozi's thought in a fairly comprehensive light.

Governing through non-action is not a conspiracy, opposites complementing each other is not a conspiracy, and cultivating strength quietly is not a conspiracy—for the simple reason that Laozi was never a schemer.
With this, I have presented Laozi's thought in a fairly comprehensive light.

zh: 庄子的哲学：物物者非物
en: Zhuangzi's Philosophy: The Creator of Things Is Not a Thing

zh: 接下来，毫无疑问要讲讲庄子，庄子呢，在道家看来，教主是老子，没有把庄子当作教主，但是实际上，庄子在老子的身边，身边我不是说时间上的身边了，而是哲学思想上的身边，在他的身边就构成了一种比较完整的叫老庄哲学。他们其实隔的时间还比较长，但是构成了一种老庄哲学。这个老庄哲学，我们在看道家的他们的教主的思维，他们的宗教的一种哲学根基的时候，大概是离不开庄子的。
en: Next, we must turn to Zhuangzi. In Daoist tradition, Laozi is venerated as the supreme master while Zhuangzi is not accorded that formal title; yet philosophically speaking—standing right alongside Laozi in spirit rather than chronological time—they together forged the complete edifice known as Lao-Zhuang philosophy. Although they were separated by a considerable span of time, they forged a unified philosophical lineage. Whenever we examine the foundational thinking of Daoist masters and the intellectual bedrock of Daoist spirituality, it is virtually impossible to separate it from Zhuangzi.

zh: 庄子，我想讲短一点，因为老子我讲的比较长了。反正大家知道，我在《北大授课》这本书里边，专门写了庄子的一些文章，而且不断地在论庄子、抄庄子。抄庄子就是把庄子的东西写成书法，《逍遥游》我是用草书写的，还翻译庄子，这个读者都不难找到，所以，我庄子可以讲得比较简略一点了。我因为非常喜欢庄子，一讲有可能在篇幅上失度了，讲着讲着就又讲多了。
en: Regarding Zhuangzi, I intend to keep my remarks concise, since I spent considerable time on Laozi. As you may know, in my book "Lectures at Peking University" I wrote dedicated essays on Zhuangzi, continually discussing and transcribing his works. By transcribing Zhuangzi, I mean rendering his texts in calligraphy—I transcribed "Carefree Wandering" in cursive script and translated his works, all of which readers can readily find; thus I can treat Zhuangzi more succinctly here. Because of my immense love for Zhuangzi, once I start, I risk losing all sense of brevity and expanding far too much.

反正大家知道，我在《北大授课》这本书里边，专门写了庄子的一些文章，而且不断地在论庄子、抄庄子。
抄庄子就是把庄子的东西写成书法，《逍遥游》我是用草书写的，还翻译庄子，这个读者都不难找到，所以，我庄子可以讲得比较简略一点了。
我因为非常喜欢庄子，一讲有可能在篇幅上失度了，讲着讲着就又讲多了。

enSentences.text: Regarding Zhuangzi, I intend to keep my remarks concise, since I spent considerable time on Laozi.
As you may know, in my book "Lectures at Peking University" I wrote dedicated essays on Zhuangzi, continually discussing and transcribing his works.

By transcribing Zhuangzi, I mean rendering his texts in calligraphy—I transcribed "Carefree Wandering" in cursive script and translated his works, all of which readers can readily find; thus I can treat Zhuangzi more succinctly here.
Because of my immense love for Zhuangzi, once I start, I risk losing all sense of brevity and expanding far too much.

zh: 大家还记得我曾经把先秦诸子的文学品相做了个排位，我把庄子放在第一位了，孟子第二，老子第三，孔子第四，这大家还有印象。伟大的孔子那么了不起，你怎么放到第四，我还讲了理由，因为我们不是从哲学思维和影响力上来讲，我们是从文学品味上来讲。庄子，以一个小孩的陌生的眼光，提出很多问题，而不是在高台上回答很多问题，他是提出问题的，然后以小孩的方式做整体的回答，这就是个艺术家了，而且用的方式是寓言，寓言，寓言，有好多好多寓言，是个大艺术家。
en: You may recall that I once ranked the literary caliber of the pre-Qin masters: placing Zhuangzi first, Mencius second, Laozi third, and Confucius fourth—a ranking many of you likely remember. People asked how the towering figure of Confucius could be ranked fourth, and I explained my reasoning: this was evaluated not by philosophical influence or social impact, but strictly by literary aesthetics and flavor. Zhuangzi looked at reality with the fresh, unjaded eyes of a child, raising boundless questions rather than preaching answers from an ivory dais; he posed questions and responded with childlike wholeness—a true artist who spoke through allegories, parables, and endless mythic narratives—a supreme literary artist.

zh: 我呢，特别强调在庄子哲学里边的两个概念，一个概念，大家可能比较陌生的，说起来有点绕口，少少的五个字里边有三个是同一个字，叫物质的物，他的哲学概念叫“物物者非物”，这就是庄子的一个非常重要的概念。
en: I wish to emphasize two concepts in Zhuangzi's philosophy: the first may sound unfamiliar and somewhat tongue-twisting, where three out of five characters are the same word for material things—his philosophical dictum that "the creator of things is not a thing" (wù wù zhě fēi wù)—a truly pivotal concept in Zhuangzi's thought.

enSentences.text: I wish to emphasize two concepts in Zhuangzi's philosophy: the first may sound unfamiliar and somewhat tongue-twisting, where three out of five characters are the same word for material things—his philosophical dictum that "the creator of things is not a thing" (wù wù zhě fēi wù)—a truly pivotal concept in Zhuangzi's thought.

zh: 什么叫“物物者非物”？第一个物是动词，它指的是创造事物的一种力量，物物者，就创造事物的人，创造物质的人，他本身不是物质。“物物者非物”，大家能够理解我讲的意思吗？让物成为物的那种力量，本身并不是物。也就是我们要成为造物者，造物者不是物，这个观念我们一定要认真地体会一下。
en: What does "the creator of things is not a thing" mean? The first "wu" functions as a verb, denoting the creative force that brings things into being; the "creator of things"—the one who generates material phenomena—is not itself a material object. "The creator of things is not a thing"—can you grasp the essence of what I mean? The transcendent power that causes things to become things is not itself a physical thing. In other words, we ought to become spiritual creators, and a creator is never a mere object—a profound concept that we must reflect upon deeply.

zh: 他在《秋水篇》里边专门讲了个概念，他的概念如果用我们现在的话讲，就是我们要以人的立场来看物，不要以物的立场来看物。什么叫以物的立场来看物？就是我的存款是300万，他的存款是400万，以此来判断我们的等级的话，就是以物论物了。庄子说不，我们要以道来论物，以人来论物，这个观念是庄子的一个重要思维。
en: In the "Autumn Floods" chapter, he expounds a concept which, phrased in contemporary terms, urges us to view things from the human perspective, rather than evaluating human life from the perspective of material things. What does it mean to view things from the standpoint of material things? It means assessing our human hierarchy by declaring: "My bank savings are 3 million, while his are 4 million"—judging human worth purely by the calculus of material possessions. Zhuangzi insists: no, we must evaluate things through the Dao and through human spiritual dignity—this is one of Zhuangzi's most vital teachings.
